contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, the contracts schema
The dispatch and the GrantDispatch transaction
Store.Commit: one transaction, the RPC inventory, codes
Run states of one seat run
Ticket statuses and the transition table
Who retries what, and whether an attempt is charged

pointers.shared: Every shape this volume names, as JSON Schema 2020-12; node schemas $ref ../../shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/NAME
The record envelope (identity, time, kind, code, node, epoch, seq)
Who the caller is: principals, peer credentials, role derivation (written beside this volume in book 1.1.0)
How the retry layers compose and the budgets they spend (written beside this volume in book 1.1.0)
N-01 implements Store.Commit, Store.Do, Tail and Snapshot
N-02 owns the leases table and its statements
N-03 owns the tickets and claims tables and their statements

purpose.s: Book 1.0.0 defined each cross-node shape in the producer, again in each consumer and a third time in prose; they disagreed (review findings F02, F03, F04, F05, F12, F14, F16, F17; shared/review-dispositions.xml).

The rule from 1.1.0: a shape, key, state machine, transition table or default that crosses a DAG edge is defined here once; a node volume cites the anchor and adds only what is specific to it; a node schema $refs contracts.schema.json and never restates a def.

Status codes everywhere: a stale or non-current lease token is 412 (reason stale_token or lease_not_current); 409 is only an entity version conflict (reason version or id) or idempotency_mismatch; 403 is authorization (record.refused, shared/authority.xml#role-derivation); 423 is a hold or a lock; 429 is a cap.

roles.s: A ticket has a phase (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/phase: worker, reviewer, spec, gate) and each phase is run by one role (#/$defs/role); phase_role pins the pairs. Status (#ticket-transitions) and phase are separate columns of the tickets table.
roles.role-def: Writes the change in its workspace; the service pushes and opens the PR (N-16 close-out); a seat never pushes.
Reads the PR head read-only and writes review.passed or review.changes.
Writes a ticket-set draft for a cut request; CR tickets hold only this phase.

A code run (N-23 plan, N-24 pods, N-25 status post), never a seat; it holds a seat-class lease so fencing and the transition table apply, and counts against gate.runs_in_flight_max, not caps.max_seats.
roles.s: Principal roles (owner, service, launcher, seat; #/$defs/principal_role) are a different axis: who is calling, derived from the peer uid (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation). A seat principal never reaches the store socket.

dispatch.s: Shape: contracts.schema.json#/$defs/dispatch_body. N-07 writes it; N-13, N-14 and N-15 read it; every consumer $refs the def (closes P01, P02). The record is envelope (kind dispatch, code 100, node N-07) plus this body.
The run id is the dispatch id: one dispatch is one run; a rerun is a new dispatch under a new token. N-13 (seat.bundle), N-14 (workspace) and N-15 (run:, seat.result) all key by it.

deadline_at is granted_at plus run.deadline_seconds.ROLE (#timing); the brief lives only in the run bundle at brief_path (N-13); build_mode is the flag:build_mode entity read in the same transaction with its version.

GrantDispatch is one Store.Do transaction by N-07 (#batch): guards of #lease-machine row GrantDispatch, then statement leases.grant (lease reserved, new token, generation plus one, holder the dispatch id, expires_at now plus start.grace_seconds), statement tickets.transition (ready or pr_open to in_flight), the lease.granted record (node N-02, by N-07) and the dispatch record; all or nothing. A dispatch without its lease, or a lease without its dispatch, cannot exist (closes F05 holder race: holder is set at grant and never empty).

The token in the operation key is known before commit: the counter:lease_token entity's version is the last issued token; N-07 proposes token = version plus 1 with a precondition on that version, and a concurrent grant makes the Commit 409 version and the next tick retries.

operation-keys.s: Form: node/operation/subject/rREVISION, pattern contracts.schema.json#/$defs/operation_key. One key per intended effect: bundle, workspace, result, push, PR and verdict of one run are six effects with six keys (closes F02, where all six shared the dispatch id).

The node segment must equal the node the authenticated caller may act as (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation), else 403 principal_mismatch. The idempotency row stores key, kind, node and request_hash: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the commit request with every record's id, at, seq and hash removed, so an honest retry that minted a new id and at hashes the same.

Same key, same hash: replay the stored commit_reply with code 200 reason replayed and write nothing. Same key, different hash: 409 idempotency_mismatch before any write or effect. The revision is the only way to make a second effect for one subject on purpose (an owner-ordered rerun is r2).

Every Commit carries a key; the table below is the complete list of operations that write. A node volume names its operations by these rows; a key form not listed is a defect (check C25 parses the rows: examples match the pattern and are unique).

batch.s: The store API (closes F04, F07). The real proto today, scheduler/api/scheduler/v1/scheduler.proto, has Executor{Run, Health} and Scheduler{Health, Status, Reload, Drain, Retry}, and nothing streams. The book adds coq.store.v1.Store{Commit, Get, List, Tail, Snapshot, Health}, coq.lease.v1.Lease{Renew, Release, Start} and coq.intake.v1.Intake{Answer} (planned files under scheduler/api/, nodes/N-01/spec.xml). Tail replaces every "Subscribe" of book 1.0.0; Put survives only as a Commit with one record.

Store.Commit (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/commit_request, reply #/$defs/commit_reply) is one SQLite transaction on the single writer, in this order: (1) authenticate the peer by SO_PEERCRED and derive role, node and permitted kinds (403 unknown_principal, kind_not_permitted, principal_mismatch, capability_expired); (2) idempotency by operation key and request hash (#operation-keys); (3) fence the lease named in the request (#fencing; 412); (4) check every precondition (entity at version, or absent at 0; 412 precondition); (5) entity compare-and-swap writes (409 version); (6) owner-registered statements on node-owned tables (#statements); (7) append 0 to 16 records, each validated against its kind's schema and the live code table (400); (8) insert outbox effects (#outbox); (9) write the idempotency row; (10) COMMIT; (11) notify Tail.

Limits per Commit: 32 entity writes, 64 statement rows, 16 records, 8 effects, 250 ms inside the transaction, no network or disk I/O other than SQLite inside it; over a limit is 422 limits before BEGIN. A request with no record and no entity write is 400.

In-process callers (every node hosted by coq-service) use Store.Do(ctx, op, fn(*Tx)) with the same steps: Tx offers Get, CAS, Delete, Next(counter), Append, Exec(statement), Fence(lease_key, token) and Effect; fn runs inside the transaction and must not do I/O. Socket callers (the launcher N-15, the owner CLI) send commit_request; the server runs the same steps.

Error mapping on the wire (google.rpc.Status with ErrorInfo reason): 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, 409 ABORTED, 412 FAILED_PRECONDITION, 422 INVALID_ARGUMENT (limits), 423 and 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, 503 UNAVAILABLE. Compatibility is additive only.

statements.s: A node-owned table is written only through a statement its owner registers here: a named, parameterized SQL statement (table.verb) with its guards, run by Exec inside a Commit. No free SQL crosses the socket or the Tx. A statement may append the owner's record kind; that record's node is the owner and its by is the caller (lease.granted is node N-02, by N-07).
callers lists who may run it; any other caller is 403 kind_not_permitted.
statements.statement-def: reserved to running; run:RUN_ID moves in the same Commit
N-12 appends stall in the same Commit
Refuses a (from, to) pair not in #ticket-transitions or a caller other than the row's owner, 412 precondition
the only writer of every flag row (hold, build_mode, freeze); N-29 rulings and N-42 controls reach it as ruling effects

lease-machine.s: One leases table (shared/state-store.xml#table-leases, row shape contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_row); there is no lease:KEY entity. class is seat (a ticket phase, key ticket:phase:attempt, granted only by GrantDispatch), work (merge.lock, publish:drive, cutover:run, unlanded:run, exittest) or maintenance (node:N-xx leader keys, watcher/PAGE, backup, cleanup, workspace, seat, tier, drain). state is reserved, running, released, expired or revoked; the token is an INTEGER from counter:lease_token and only grows; holder is never empty.

generation bumps only on grant (each row below whose effect says new token); version bumps on every write. Renew never moves the generation, so "renew only for the current generation" of book 1.0.0 is gone; currency is the token and the state.

Hold (flag:hold set): GrantDispatch and work-class Acquire are refused 423 reason hold; maintenance Acquire is allowed, so watchers, the leader, backups, cleanup and drains run under a hold (closes the F05 watcher-down-for-good case). The desired set N-07 computes is: tickets ready (or pr_open awaiting reviewer or gate) with not_before passed and no reserved or running lease for the ticket and phase; it is computed under a hold too, and only the grant is refused.

Re-grant of the same key happens only for a free regrant (failure kinds claim_overlap, files-claimed, cap, workspace.refused, or a start-grace expiry; #retry-owner), always with a new token. Every charged failure moves to attempt n+1, a new key.
Rows: from lists one or more states separated by spaces (absent: no row for the key); caller is the node that runs the statement; guard is checked at commit; a failed guard is the code in brackets.

lease-transition.guard: class seat; ticket ready (or pr_open for reviewer and gate) at the read version; no reserved or running lease for the ticket and phase; seats reserved or running below caps.max_seats; ticket budget left (shared/retry-budget.xml#budgets); flag:hold absent [423 hold, 429 cap, 412 precondition]
lease-transition.effect: new token; generation 1; holder the dispatch id; expires_at now plus start.grace_seconds; same Commit as the dispatch record and tickets.transition to in_flight

lease-transition.guard: as above, and the row's last end was a free regrant recorded by N-11 (N-11/regrant key) [412 precondition]
lease-transition.effect: new token; generation plus 1; new holder; expires_at now plus start.grace_seconds

lease-transition.guard: class maintenance [423 when another holder is reserved or running]
lease-transition.effect: new token; generation plus 1; holder node and job; expires_at now plus lease.ttl_seconds (leader: lease.leader_ttl_seconds)

lease-transition.guard: class work; flag:hold absent [423 hold], except merge.lock while bootstrap mode is on (cut-over.xml#bootstrap-merge); no other holder [423]
lease-transition.effect: new token; generation plus 1; holder node and job; expires_at now plus lease.ttl_seconds (merge.lock: merge.lock_seconds)

lease-transition.guard: token matches; now before expires_at [412 stale_token, 412 lease_not_current]
lease-transition.effect: run_id set; heartbeat_at now; expires_at now plus lease.ttl_seconds; same Commit as run:RUN_ID spawning to running
heartbeat_at only; expires_at keeps the start grace
heartbeat_at, progress_at; expires_at now plus lease.ttl_seconds

lease-transition.guard: now at or past expires_at at commit
lease-transition.effect: ended_at; end_reason start-grace; lease.expired; no attempt is charged (N-11 free regrant)

lease-transition.guard: now at or past expires_at at commit
lease-transition.effect: ended_at; end_reason expired; lease.expired; N-12 writes the kill and N-11 charges per #retry-owner stall

lease-transition.guard: row version equals the version N-12 judged and the stall predicate still holds at commit [409 version: a fresh heartbeat wins]
lease-transition.effect: ended_at; end_reason revoked-stall, revoked-launcher-lost or revoked-ruling; token unchanged; same Commit as the kill entity (#kill-authority)

fencing.s: A Commit that acts under a lease carries lease {key, token} (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_ref). It is current only when, at commit, the row for that key is reserved or running, its token equals the presented token and now is before expires_at. A token that differs is 412 stale_token; a matching token on a released, expired or revoked row, or past expires_at, is 412 lease_not_current; both write record.stale and the writer exits.

Fencing is by lease key, never by (ticket, attempt): worker attempt 1 and reviewer attempt 1 are different keys, and a system job fences with its system key (closes NF-A3). Every seat-run write (bundle, workspace, run start, renew, result, close-out) and every work-class job write carries its lease.

terminal-report.s: seat.result or phase.failed carrying the most recent token of a lease that is now revoked or expired is accepted once per run_id with fenced: true (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/failure_body); its operation key (N-15/seat.result/RUN_ID/r1) makes a second report a replay or a 409 idempotency_mismatch.

N-11 treats a fenced report as an echo: the failure was already charged by the stall or expiry path that ended the lease; the report adds evidence (cost, turns, terminal reason) and changes no ticket status. An older token than the row's is still 412 stale_token. This closes NF4: a killed run's result lands, no result.pending card is raised for it.

kill-authority.s: N-12 decides: it writes entity kill:RUN_ID {reason, lease_version, at} in the same Commit as Revoke (key N-12/kill/RUN_ID@LEASE_VERSION/r1). An owner kill (an N-42 Kill action or an answered card) reaches N-12 as the N-29 ruling effect run.kill with scope all-running or run; USERHALT is a hold (flag:hold through N-44), not a kill, and running seats finish or stall out under it. Nobody else writes a kill.

The launcher (N-15) executes: it watches kill:* for its runs and stops the per-run unit coq-seat-RUN_ID; the unit's ExecStop is coq-seat-exec kill RUN_ID (shared/authority.xml#principals), which writes 1 to the unit's cgroup.kill, because a user manager running as coq-launch cannot signal processes of a seat uid. TimeoutStopSec is kill.grace_seconds. The deadline is the unit's RuntimeMaxSec, so no second timer kills.

When the launcher is gone (its heartbeat entity older than 3 x lease.heartbeat_seconds), N-12 (principal coq-svc) runs coq-seat-exec kill RUN_ID itself, the same cross-user verb. kill.grace_seconds is the one grace everywhere (#timing).

run-states.s: Entity run:RUN_ID, written by compare-and-swap before and after each step, so a restarted launcher resumes every run from its entity, never from a directory scan. Each seat runs in its own transient unit, systemd-run --user --unit=coq-seat-RUN_ID --collect -p KillMode=control-group -p TimeoutStopSec=kill.grace_seconds -p RuntimeMaxSec=BOUND, outside the service cgroup, so a service restart does not kill seats and the launcher adopts a run by its unit name; the unit name also makes a second launch of one run impossible (closes NF-A11).
Output: stdout to result.json.partial; on exit the launcher validates it, renames it to result.json, fsyncs, and writes result.ok holding its sha256.

run-transition.trigger: seat.bundle and workspace both committed for the dispatch; CAS expected absent; then systemd-run
the unit is active with a main pid; same Commit as lease Start (N-15/run.start)
systemd-run failed, or no active unit by start.grace_seconds; the lease is released; failure_kind crashed to N-11
the unit went inactive (exit, kill or RuntimeMaxSec)
seat.result committed (N-15/seat.result), fenced when the lease had ended (#terminal-report); no valid result.json is terminal_reason no_result
the phase close-out committed (pr.open, ticket-set.draft or review.verdict) or the failure was handed to N-11; the slot is freed

ticket-transitions.s: Statuses: contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ticket_status. Terminal: done, dead, cancelled, refused; the only way out of a terminal status is dead to waiting by an owner ruling. merged means merged on main and not yet verified; merged to done happens only when N-10 writes verified for a main sha that contains the merge (F13).

This table is the only transition list in the book; node volumes cite rows. tickets.transition (#statements) refuses any pair not here, a caller other than owner, or a from status that is no longer current, with 412 precondition and record ticket.transition_refused. claims says what the same Commit does to the ticket's claims (#claims): acquire, keep, release or none.

Notes. in_flight to ready is the free regrant (no attempt charged). retry_wait to ready fires when the attempt's not_before passes. pr_open to in_flight dispatches the reviewer or gate phase on the open PR; in_flight to pr_open on review.passed returns it (N-19 close-out). in_flight to done closes a CR ticket: the ticket-set.accepted Commit (N-18) whose source_request names the CR. in_flight to waiting is harness_mismatch (#retry-owner), with one card. dead to waiting needs an owner ruling (ticket.unblock, N-29) and resets the attempt counter; claims are taken again at the next ready. A main red after merged holds merges (N-10) and cuts a fix ticket; the merged ticket stays merged until a verified main contains it.

claims.s: One authority: the claims table owned by N-03 (shared/state-store.xml#table-claims: id, ticket, pattern, prefix, taken_at, released_at). The N-14 file_claims table of book 1.0.0 is deleted; N-14 only verifies that the dispatch's ticket holds live claims covering its files (412 claim_missing).

prefix is the literal part of the pattern before its first glob metacharacter. Two claims overlap when either prefix starts with the other (two-way containment): herdr/bin/ and herdr/bin/seat.sh overlap. Acquire runs inside the Commit of the transition whose claims attribute is acquire: it reads the live claims (released_at null) of other tickets, refuses the whole Commit on any overlap (412 precondition; the ticket stays waiting with reason files-claimed) and inserts one row per pattern. The ticket's own claims are excluded from the check, so a retried ticket never blocks on itself (closes NF6).

Release sets released_at by statement in the Commit of a release transition; a released row is never reused and a reacquire inserts new rows, so there is no primary-key collision on a path (closes NF-A6, NF5). The overlap check is a scan of live claims, bounded by the statement row limit (#batch); a non-unique partial index on prefix where released_at is null serves it.

retry-owner.s: The only table of who retries a failure and whether an attempt is charged (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers composes the layers). Only the innermost layer retries a given failure; an outer layer sees it only when the inner one gives up. Every failure routed to N-11 carries contracts.schema.json#/$defs/failure_body and N-11 accepts every failure_kind.

charges: yes (N-11 charges attempt n+1 at once), no (free: regrant or wait, the attempt counter does not move), on-exhaust (the owner retries inside its own budget; on give-up it writes the failure to N-11, which charges once). session: new (a fresh seat session), resume-if-done (resume the worker session only when the prior worker run ended done, else new), none (no seat is dispatched by this row).
retry-owner.retry-row: close-out recovery in code, 3 tries, no model; then phase.failed to N-11
the fenced seat.result that follows is an echo
free regrant on the next tick with capacity
worker phase attempt n+1; the gate phase is never re-dispatched after N-25 has given up
a reviewer whose PR head moved (N-19 head check): nothing charged; the ticket returns in_flight to pr_open and the new head's green gate leads to a new reviewer grant
ticket to waiting with one card; nothing dispatches until the harness pin matches
no ladder climb; a defect record and one card (shared/ci-capacity.xml#admission)
retry-owner.s: Attempts: worker, reviewer and spec-author 3 each; dead after the third charged failure of a phase. Per-ticket and daily budgets (budget.* keys, #timing) are enforced by N-07 at GrantDispatch.

outbox.s: An external effect (forge push, PR, merge, status post, Jenkins build, kubernetes object, ntfy push, Drive upload) is an effects row (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/effect_row; table shared/state-store.xml#table-effects) written in the same Commit as the record that decides it, with state intent. Nothing calls a provider before that Commit.

A worker of the deciding node sends it, records the provider's id (external_id) and reads the provider back; each state move is effects.advance by compare-and-swap: intent, sent, accepted (provider took it), done (read back observed), failed (after 3 attempts, routed per #retry-owner). A send whose outcome is unknown (timeout, lost reply, crash) moves to unknown and is looked up by op_id at the provider before any resend.

Lookup keys: Jenkins builds carry the parameter COQ_OP_ID; the worker searches the queue and the builds for it before any repost (a queue item URL expires after 5 minutes, so the build parameter is the identity). A merge is found by GET of the PR (merged, merge_commit_sha); a status by the statuses of the sha for its context; a PR by its head branch; a push by the remote head sha; an ntfy push by its message id. No record claims an effect done before the read back (invariant I06).

epoch-cursor.s: seq is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT on records: unique and strictly increasing within one store file, never reused, and not gapless (retention deletes rows; a rolled-back transaction can leave a gap). No reader counts seqs.

Entity store:epoch (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/store_epoch) names the epoch, when and why it began, and min_retained_seq (advanced by N-45 in the same Commit that deletes rows). Records (envelope epoch), Tail frames and cursors (#/$defs/cursor) carry the epoch; a seq means nothing outside its epoch.

Tail(cursor) answers cursor.expired when the cursor's epoch is not current, its seq is below min_retained_seq or above the high-water seq; the client then takes Snapshot, which returns its class's state and the seq S read in one read transaction, and tails strictly after S. Append-only kinds apply idempotently by record id. Entity-only frames carry the entity key and version, no seq, and coalesce by key (#entity-only).

restore.s: Restore of the store from a verified backup (STATE/backup/store/, nodes/N-05/spec.xml), bound restore.rto_minutes; the data loss is bounded by backup.rpo_offhost_hours for a host loss and by backup.interval_seconds otherwise.
restore.step: Stop coq-service; copy the backup to STATE/store/coq.db; integrity_check; start the service in restore mode, which accepts no socket caller but the owner until step 6.

First Commit (N-01/store.restored/EPOCH/r1): store:epoch to epoch plus 1, cause restored; flag:hold set with reason restore and flag:build_mode off, both through the N-44 flags package (statement flags.set run in restore mode, the one flag writer); counter:lease_token raised by 1000000000 so no token issued after the backup is ever reissued; every reserved or running lease to expired.

Reconcile before any effect: N-04 polls the forge fresh; N-09 records merges found on main after the backup's main sha; N-23 looks up Jenkins builds by COQ_OP_ID; every effects row in intent, sent or unknown becomes unknown and is looked up (#outbox); tickets in_flight move to retry_wait uncharged and pr_open tickets are matched to their PRs.
store.restored 200 names the new epoch, the backup id, its high-water seq and what reconciliation found; every Tail client gets cursor.expired and resnapshots.
The line stays held; only an owner ruling (N-29, applied by N-44) clears the hold. A restore never releases its own hold.

timing.s: The one table of timing and capacity defaults. The same keys and values are the config-key defaults of shared/state-store.xml#config-keys; a node volume cites the key, never the number. The budget keys mean what shared/retry-budget.xml#budgets says; their values are owner-tunable defaults.

entity-only.s: Kinds registered entity-only write their entity by compare-and-swap and append no record unless the state changes: tick:SUBKIND (a record only for tick.missed), health:service (a record on a status transition), heartbeats (a record only for adopted or a token change), page.state (a record only on a state change; N-32), watcher.alive (a record when the lamp changes; N-27), pushed.frame (a record only on connect, resync and drop; N-31). This closes NF-A7 and NF-D6: book 1.0.0 made every entity write a record, about 29 million rows a year.

The kind registry (shared/record-kinds.xml, generated) carries storage="entity-only" and the coalesce-key from the owning node's emits row; a record of an entity-only kind outside a state change is 400. Tail streams entity-only changes as coalesced entity frames (#epoch-cursor).

many-agents.readers: Every node volume and schema cites these anchors and $refs contracts.schema.json; the review seat reads this volume first when two nodes disagree.
many-agents.writers: A change here is one PR that also changes every node volume citing the changed row; check C24 parses the ticket transitions and C25 the operation keys, and C22 validates the examples.
many-agents.collision: Two GrantDispatch commits for one ticket and phase: the second fails the no-live-lease guard or the counter precondition (409 version) and the next tick sees the first. A renew racing a revoke: the revoke's version guard fails (409), the fresh heartbeat wins. Two commits under one operation key: one row, the other replays 200 or is 409 idempotency_mismatch. A stale token: 412. None of these waits and none overwrites.
many-agents.test: Planned N-01 test: 20 goroutines Commit one operation key, exactly one row and 19 replays; the six effects of one run under six keys all commit (AT-F02). Planned N-02 test: 20 GrantDispatch on one ticket, one lease, 19 refusals; renew between stall snapshot and revoke keeps the lease (AT-F05). Status: not-run.
